EX-99.1 2 gmab_20261028xex99d1.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Genmab Announces Statistically Significant, Clinically Meaningful Improvement in Overall Survival and Objective Response with Petosemtamab Combination at First Interim Analysis in First-Line R/M Patients with PD-L1+ Head and Neck Cancer Company Announcement COPENHAGEN, Denmark; October 28, 2026 • Phase 3 LiGeR-HN1 trial of Petosemtamab in combination with pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab alone met both primary endpoints, reducing the risk of death by 50% in patients with PD-L1 positive head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), regardless of HPV status • Genmab plans to engage global regulatory authorities and will submit full results for presentation at a future medical meeting Genmab A/S (Nasdaq: GMAB) today announced positive topline results from the global Phase 3 LiGeR-HN1 trial ( NCT06525220 ) evaluating petosemtamab, an investigational IgG1-bispecific antibody targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and the leucine-rich repeat containing G-protein-coupled receptor 5 (LGR5), in combination with pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab in patients with first-line (1L) PD-L1 positive recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC).

Based on the first interim analysis assessed by an independent data monitoring committee (IDMC), treatment with the petosemtamab combination demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in overall survival (OS), reducing the risk of death by 50%, and objective response rate (ORR) versus pembrolizumab [OS: HR 0.50 (95% CI, 0.37, 0.67); p<0.0001; ORR: odds ratio 3.17 (95% CI, 2.06, 4.89; p<0.0001), meeting its dual primary endpoints, regardless of HPV status.

“Meeting its dual primary endpoints of overall survival and objective response rate at the first interim analysis underscores the potential of petosemtamab plus pembrolizumab to transform first-line treatment for patients with PD-L1-positive disease, regardless of HPV status.

These results suggest this chemotherapy-free combination could reshape the treatment of this devastating disease by establishing a new therapeutic option.” “These topline Phase 3 results represent a defining milestone for Genmab and further strengthen our conviction in petosemtamab as a potential first-in-class treatment option for patients with this difficult-to-treat cancer,” said Jan van de Winkel, Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Genmab.

The LiGeR-HN1 topline findings mark an important step toward potentially bringing petosemtamab to patients with recurrent or metastatic head and neck cancer, and we look forward to engaging with regulatory authorities globally and sharing the full dataset with the medical community.” Based on these positive topline results, Genmab plans to engage global regulatory authorities and will submit the full results from LiGeR-HN1 for presentation at a future medical meeting.
